role: Independent Apple HIG typography/accessibility reviewer; not Apple affiliation or certification
scope: Current web specimen on desktop, with conditional integration guidance for macOS/iOS/iPadOS. No other Apple platforms assumed.
independence: No prior reports or other reviewers read before initial report.

tests.method: Read current index.html, demo.css, demo.js, dist/tabuna.css independently
tests.result: Scoped custom font, semantic labels/headings, real UI sample, auto opsz, dark palette, focus-visible style confirmed.

tests.method: Separate local IAB tab, http://127.0.0.1:8876, 1280x720; read computed DOM and visually inspect reading section

result.heading: 43.52px/500; line-height 47.0016px
result.body_preset: 18px/400; line-height 28.8px; normal tracking; auto optical sizing

tests.result: Status changes to Настройки образца сохранены.

tests.method: WCAG relative luminance arithmetic from CSS solid text and background colors
tests.limit: Computed palette contrast only, not rasterized thin-stroke legibility or complete accessibility audit.

reasons: Real 16px Tabuna UI label/checkbox and 500 button are demonstrated; keyboard action updates status.
Target-device small-type rasterization and native larger text/Bold Text integration remain unverified.
Rendered 43.52px/500 heading is clear and unclipped at the observed desktop viewport.
No full size/weight, narrow-window, or text enlargement sweep performed.
16px/400 article with 1.65 line height and 18px/400 body preset with 1.6 line height provide practical starting settings.
Only a short sample and one rendered desktop context were assessed.
No human timed reading, comprehension, or fatigue data collected.

findings.condition: Using this web demo as proof of native Apple UI readiness
findings.evidence: Distribution provides CSS @font-face and opt-in .tabuna; no native Dynamic Type or Bold Text integration is demonstrated. Browser UI controls really use Tabuna at 16px/400 and button at 500.
findings.recommendation: Keep UI readiness conditional; for each intended Apple native target map custom fonts to semantic text styles and test larger accessibility sizes and Bold Text.
findings.acceptance_test: In a native sample, exercise all supported Dynamic Type categories and Bold Text with Russian/English labels, values, and actions; verify text remains readable and actions reachable without clipping.
findings.basis: Apple guidance requires accessible custom-font integration; missing native sample is an evidence limit, not proof that this font cannot support it.

findings.condition: Text-size enlargement or narrow windows in the demo
findings.evidence: demo.js update() writes inline pixel sizes to #sample-text; hero h1 has white-space:nowrap; only 1280x720 default size was rendered in this bounded review. Body article itself uses 1rem and unitless 1.65.
findings.recommendation: Validate browser text enlargement separately from specimen size control, including narrow windows; use adaptive wrapping and relative type integration if any clipping occurs.
findings.acceptance_test: At 320 CSS px and text enlargement through 200%, all control labels and reading content remain usable without loss; document any intentional horizontal scrolling inside code/specimen only.
findings.basis: Product acceptance test derived from HIG adaptation principles; 320/200% are review test conditions, not claimed Apple numeric mandates.

findings.condition: Claiming suitability for sustained reading from this specimen
findings.evidence: The reading sample has two short Russian paragraphs at 16px/400 with 26.4px line height; body preset is 18px/400 with 28.8px line height. No timed reader study was performed.
findings.recommendation: Run sustained Russian and English reading sessions across target displays and accessibility needs before claiming comfort, comprehension, or parity with the system font.
findings.acceptance_test: Record corpus, duration, device, viewing scale, participant characteristics, comprehension/error measures, and fatigue responses under a predeclared protocol; do not substitute outline metrics for reader results.
findings.basis: Review evidence requirement informed by Apple instruction to test legibility in context; study design is reviewer recommendation.

findings.condition: Integrators choose Thin/ExtraLight for small functional text because the full axis is advertised
findings.evidence: Weight axis permits 100–900 and the demo offers every weight; UI/body presets appropriately use 500/400 and introductory body guidance recommends 400.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the current regular/medium defaults and add an explicit small-UI caution around thin weights in integration guidance.
findings.acceptance_test: Document a recommended 400–600 starting range for small UI, subject to device testing; if lighter weights are used, verify intended size/contrast with readers.
findings.basis: Apple cautions that thin custom-font weights may require larger sizes; 400–600 is a local starting recommendation rather than a HIG rule.

limits: Bounded initial review; no font/source edits.
Official HIG page direct opens returned JavaScript shells; live official search-index excerpts and bundled HIG routing references supplied contextual guidance.
No font outline/hinting audit, native application test, VoiceOver session, mobile/zoom or dark-mode screenshot run.
Browser AX exposure is not equivalent to an assistive-technology user test.
No claim of human study, HIG certification, or long-reading fitness.
